subject: Visibility & Ops: dashboards, trace hooks, and alert-routing check-ins

To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Visibility & Ops: dashboards, trace hooks, and alert-routing check-ins

Hi Laura / Marissa —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. Our engineering leadership is aligned that we need a lightweight but actionable observability rollout for the next sprint (2 weeks). High level asks from Kepler:

- A concise set of dashboards showing model latency / error rates (per endpoint and model version)
- Tracing hooks around inference calls to link request_id -> customer session
- An error taxonomy so we can route actionable items to Eng vs. SRE vs. Product
- Alert routing rules and a basic runbook for on-call triage

We want to avoid a big lift — prefer an initial "minimum viable observability" plan that we can iterate on. Could your team share a short checklist and any templated runbook/alert mapping you recommend?

I've attached our internal incident playbook (ops@keplerhealth.com) and we can share access to our Grafana account if needed. Proposed kick-off: Friday 10am PT. Will that work?

Thanks,
Ava

Hi Ava —

Friday 10am PT works for us. We'll use that time for a short alignment followed by a scoped checklist we can commit to for the two-week sprint. Quick notes on what we'll bring:

- A proposed "MV Observability" checklist (dashboards, trace points, error labels, alert tiers)
- A draft runbook template that maps an incoming alert -> ownership queue -> triage steps
- Example tracing snippet for your SDK (single-line instrumentation to attach request_id)
- Signal map PDF (shows which metric/trace/error goes to which alert)

1) Ava / Kepler: share Grafana/Prometheus read-only link OR sample metrics export (preferred), and one example request_id from a recent failed request.
2) Kepler: confirm which teams should receive high/medium/low alerts (Eng, SRE, Product).
3) Redwood: Marissa will prepare the checklist and Dev will prepare the lightweight tracing snippet we propose.

I'll attach the initial signal map and runbook draft to this thread after the alignment; please review during the call. See you Friday.

Best,

From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Visibility & Ops: dashboards, trace hooks, and alert-routing check-ins

Hi Ava / Team —

Great alignment today — appreciated the clear priorities. Follow-up summary and the "two-week MV plan" we agreed on below. I've kept items narrow so Kepler can get meaningful observability without a long integration window.

Two-week MV Observability plan (deliverables and owners):

1) Dashboards (deliverable: 3 dashboard panels) — owner: Redwood (Marissa)
   - Latency distribution by endpoint + p50/p95/p99 (panel 1)
   - Error rate by error_label, with links to example traces (panel 2)
   - Throughput / concurrency + model-version selector (panel 3)

2) Tracing hooks (deliverable: SDK patch + example trace links) — owner: Redwood (Dev)
   - Single-line SDK snippet to emit request_id and upstream session_id to Redwood tracer
   - Example ingestion: mapping trace id -> request_id in logs and dashboard drilldowns

3) Error taxonomy (deliverable: taxonomy doc + labels) — owner: Kepler + Redwood (joint)
   - Proposed initial labels: model_error, infra_error, rate_limited, validation_error, client_misuse
   - Each label maps to routing: infra_error -> SRE, model_error -> Eng, validation_error -> Product

4) Alert routing + runbook (deliverable: alert policies + 1-pg runbook) — owner: Kepler ops with Redwood template
   - High (pager): infra_error p99 spikes, system OOMs, model-serving down
   - Medium (email/Slack): model_error increase > 2x baseline for 15m
   - Low (ticket): validation_error occurrences > 5/day
   - Runbook template includes triage checklist, rollback hints, and escalation path to on-call Eng

Milestones and check-ins:
- Fri EOD (May 12): Redwood sends dashboard JSON export + SDK snippet + taxonomy draft
- Mon (May 15) morning: Kepler shares feedback; iterate
- Wed (May 17): First alert rules live in test environment

Attachments included in this email (zipped into the drive folder):
- kepler_signal_map_v0.pdf (visual mapping of signals -> alerts)
- initial_runbook_draft.md (one-page runbook template)

Notes / risks:
- If we do not get a sample request_id by EOD Friday, the tracing example will be approximated and may need an extra validation step.
- If Kepler's Grafana requires a plugin we can't access, we'll request a sample export and render dashboards in Redwood's test Grafana for validation.

Next practical step for Kepler: post the read-only Grafana link or drop a metrics export into the shared Drive folder. I'll upload the dashboard JSON and SDK snippet to the Drive by EOD.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: kepler_signal_map_v0.pdf, initial_runbook_draft.md

Thanks, team —

This looks exactly like the pragmatic plan we wanted. We'll:
- Drop a Grafana read-only link to the Drive folder by EOD (you should see it in the shared Drive).
- Confirm routing for high/medium/low as: SRE / Eng / Product (matches your proposal).
- Share a sample request_id from an error event (I'll ask the backend lead to pull one).

Marissa — appreciate the concrete threshold suggestions. If we can get the dashboard JSON and the SDK snippet in the Drive, we'll iterate quickly.

One operational ask: can Redwood include a short mapping that lists "what alert fields must be present" (e.g., request_id, model_version, host_id, trace_id) so our telemetry team can ensure payload completeness? That'll reduce back-and-forth.

I'll be online for the next few hours if you want to do a quick sync.

Best,
Ava
VP Engineering, Kepler Health
